[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Static Type Checking in Python with mypy"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Python is a dynamically typed language, meaning that the type of a variable is checked during runtime. While this offers flexibility, it can also lead to runtime errors that could have been caught earlier with static type checking. mypy is a static type checker for Python that helps you catch these errors before running your code."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Why Use Static Type Checking?"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Early Error Detection: Catch type-related errors during development, not in production."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Improved Code Readability: Type annotations make your code easier to understand."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Enhanced Code Maintainability: Refactoring becomes safer and easier with type information."},{"order":7,"type":"subheading","text":"Installation"},{"order":8,"type":"paragraph","text":"Install mypy using pip:"},{"order":9,"type":"code","text":"pip install mypy"},{"order":10,"type":"subheading","text":"Basic Usage"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"1. Add Type Hints: Use type annotations in your Python code. These annotations specify the expected type of variables, function arguments, and return values."},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"2. Run mypy: Execute mypy on your Python files to check for type errors."},{"order":13,"type":"subheading","text":"Example"},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"# example.py

def greet(name: str) -> str:
    return f"Hello, {name}"

print(greet("World"))
print(greet(123)) # This will cause a type error"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"In this example, the `greet` function expects a string argument. The second call to `greet` with an integer will be flagged as a type error by mypy."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"Running mypy"},{"order":17,"type":"code","text":"mypy example.py"},{"order":18,"type":"paragraph","text":"mypy will output an error message indicating the type mismatch:"},{"order":19,"type":"code","text":"example.py:5: error: Argument 1 to "greet" has incompatible type "int"; expected "str""},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"Type Annotations"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Python 3.6+ supports type annotations using the following syntax:"},{"order":22,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Variable Annotations: `variable: type = value`"},{"order":23,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Function Annotations: `def function(arg: type) -> return_type:`"},{"order":24,"type":"subheading","text":"Common Types"},{"order":25,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`int`: Integer"},{"order":26,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`float`: Floating-point number"},{"order":27,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`str`: String"},{"order":28,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`bool`: Boolean"},{"order":29,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`List[type]`: List of elements of a specific type (from the `typing` module)"},{"order":30,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`Dict[key_type, value_type]`: Dictionary with specific key and value types (from the `typing` module)"},{"order":31,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`Tuple[type1, type2, ...]`: Tuple with specific types for each element (from the `typing` module)"},{"order":32,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`Optional[type]`: A value that can be either of the specified type or `None` (from the `typing` module)"},{"order":33,"type":"bullet_point","text":"`Any`: Any type (use sparingly, as it defeats the purpose of type checking) (from the `typing` module)"},{"order":34,"type":"subheading","text":"Example with Typing Module"},{"order":35,"type":"code","text":"from typing import List, Dict

def process_data(items: List[int]) -> Dict[str, int]:
    result: Dict[str, int] = {}
    for item in items:
        result[str(item)] = item * 2
    return result

data: List[int] = [1, 2, 3]
processed_data: Dict[str, int] = process_data(data)
print(processed_data)"},{"order":36,"type":"subheading","text":"Configuration"},{"order":37,"type":"paragraph","text":"You can configure mypy using a `mypy.ini` file. This file allows you to specify various options, such as enabling strict mode, ignoring certain errors, and specifying the Python version."},{"order":38,"type":"code","text":"# mypy.ini

[mypy]
strict = True
python_version = 3.8"},{"order":39,"type":"subheading","text":"Ignoring Errors"},{"order":40,"type":"paragraph","text":"Sometimes, you may want to ignore specific type errors. You can do this using `# type: ignore` comments."},{"order":41,"type":"code","text":"def legacy_function(arg):
    return arg * 2  # type: ignore  # Ignore type error here"},{"order":42,"type":"subheading","text":"Conclusion"},{"order":43,"type":"paragraph","text":"Static type checking with mypy can significantly improve the quality and maintainability of your Python code. By adding type annotations and running mypy, you can catch type-related errors early in the development process, leading to more robust and reliable applications."}]
